text:
Matt Boldy has 79 shots in 18 games, more than four a night, which is why his seven goals look like a misprint. He is shooting 8.9% against a usual 14%, and he has 10.4 expected goals on his own shots. Our numbers call him due, and that is about as safe as a hockey prediction gets.

Meanwhile he is helping in other ways: a seven-game point streak (two goals, six assists) and a top line with Kirill Kaprizov and Joel Eriksson Ek that Quinn Hughes described as one where "we can tilt the ice when they're out there," per NHL.com's Heather Rule. The numbers agree. Minnesota takes 62.7% of the five-on-five expected goals with Boldy on, 12.8 points better than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his own zone with possession 70% of the time last season, and Evolving-Hockey credits him with drawing more penalties than he takes. Our projection has him near 40 goals. Getting there means a lot of pucks finally going in.
headline: Boldy's shots are piling up faster than his goals
